Ferrite developer docs · RT-950 Pro

SPI flash map

The radio's 4 MB SPI flash under Ferrite, layout 3 (decision 333): factory calibration, Ferrite's settings and records, what is planned, and the space still free. The firmware's own ranges are in layout.rs; the installer saves the whole chip to your computer first, and a layout change is moved by Ferrite Console over the link.

Pick a sector

Each square is 4 KB; a row is 128 KB. Hover or tap one to see what holds it.

Key

  • Header, settings, trims, SSB patch
  • Channels, zones, presets, waypoints
  • APRS settings, contacts, heard, messages
  • Event log
  • Scratch ring
  • Planned, not written yet
  • Held for later
  • Never written
  • Free

A dot: inside layout::WRITABLE, the only range the flash driver lets Ferrite erase or program.

Never written

  • 0x00F000–0x00FFFF: factory calibration. Back it up before anything else; Ferrite only reads it.
  • 0x300000–0x3FFFFF: the bootloader's update area. A valid header at 0x300000 (magic 0xA55A) makes the bootloader reflash the MCU from it at the next boot.
  • The flash driver refuses any erase or program outside WRITABLE, so no bug above it can reach these; the link's raw data messages are held to the same ranges (LINK-59, LINK-60).
  • The first 64 KB block holds calibration: it is only ever erased a 4 KB sector at a time (the driver has no block erase).

How records are kept

  • A fixed map: every record has one address from its number; an erased record is an empty one. No file system.
  • Settings and the APRS record: two copies, A and B, the newer valid one wins.
  • Changing a written record rewrites its sector through a scratch sector, whose footer says where it goes, so a power cut leaves the old or the new sector, never half. 32 scratch sectors take turns, so none wears out first; channel writes queued for one sector share a rewrite.
  • Rings (event log, APRS heard and messages) append into erased bytes; packed lists (waypoints, contacts) keep each sector's last 32 B free for that footer.
  • The layout header at 0x000000 names the layout; a firmware that finds another leaves the data alone until Console has moved it and stamped the header (UPD-16, LINK-62).
